issues.description: Guard predicate `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is too broad and lets the original Enter-accept path still fire
issues.detail: The new branch fires for every non-Tab key (arrows, Escape, modifiers) and is spliced before the existing item-selection guard, so the contract of which keys accept vs. dismiss is implementation-defined. Worse, the enclosing Enter/Return/Tab block can still reach the old accept logic for some items. Narrow the predicate to Return/Enter explicitly and short-circuit the accept path.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the event via `textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` leaks editor internals into the completion widget
issues.detail: Directly invoking the parent editor's handler couples the popup to the editor's exact event semantics and bypasses Qt's focus/proxy logic. The widget's contract should be accept/dismiss/ignore, not forward into another widget's input pipeline. Prefer `hide()` plus `event.ignore()` and let Qt's normal propagation deliver the key.

issues.description: Bad taste: special-case bolted onto an already-busy keyPressEvent instead of restructuring dispatch
issues.detail: The new block is a wart inside an overloaded handler. The accept-on-Enter logic should be a single predicate at the top: `is this key an accept key given config?` Computing that once removes the hide-and-replay dance and keeps the rest of the function unchanged. Good taste eliminates the special case rather than adding one.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keypress for a static user preference
issues.detail: Reading the config through the plugin conf system on every key event in the popup is a dictionary walk in the typing hot path. Cache the value when the popup is shown (store on self) or subscribe to config changes. Not catastrophic, but lazy and easy to fix.

issues.description: Awkward style `not key == Qt.Key_Tab`; write `key != Qt.Key_Tab`
issues.detail: Parses correctly but forces the reader to verify precedence in a keyPressEvent where ambiguity is most expensive. The `!=` form reads at a glance and matches surrounding code voice. Trivial fix.

issues.description: No test coverage and no comment stating the intended key-handling contract
issues.detail: Completion key handling regresses silently. Add a test that toggles the pref off, sends Enter, and asserts no completion was accepted. Pair with a one-line comment or docstring stating which keys accept, dismiss, or pass through so future subclasses can preserve the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-scoped patch for a real user problem but lands as NEEDS-WORK. The central defect is the guard `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` placed inside an overloaded Enter/Return/Tab handler: the predicate is too broad, its contract is unstated, and the original Enter-accept path is not cleanly short-circuited. Secondary issues: re-dispatching through `textedit.keyPressEvent` leaks editor internals (prefer `event.ignore()`), `get_conf` runs on every keystroke, and there are no tests or a written spec for which keys accept versus dismiss. Restructure as a single `is-accept-key?` predicate at the top of the handler, cache the config, fix the style, and add a test.
